insight.title: Your Genes Remember Events You Never Experienced
insight.subtitle: A look at how trauma and survival pass down through your biology.
insight.notificationHook: Your biology holds a family diary.

sections.text: You are carrying memories from ancestors you never met. Biology once taught that only your own experiences shaped your traits, but recent findings show that intense life events can leave chemical marks on your DNA.

These molecular tags act like switchboard toggles. When an ancestor survives a famine or intense fear, they pass down a cellular "instruction manual" that readies your own body to react to similar dangers before you are born.

This creates a biological bridge between generations. You arrive in the world with a set of internal instincts that were fine-tuned by the hardships—or the prosperity—of the people who came before you.
You are the living archive of your family’s history.

audioBrief.script:
Welcome to your Sift Daily Briefing. This is the clear, plain version of today's news.

United States lawmakers are calling for stricter rules on advanced artificial intelligence chips. This follows a new Department of Commerce rule that limits remote access to these chips. The rule targets data centers in Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, and Brazil. Officials say these locations present a high risk of technology diversion. Democratic Representative Pramila Jayapal says more oversight is needed to protect national security. Meanwhile, a House committee is investigating whether Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick blocked efforts to stop the smuggling of chips to China. The House Foreign Affairs Committee says the Trump administration approved the export of 879,000 chips to Chinese companies between December 2025 and May 2026.

Turning to technology, Nvidia has lost its spot as the third-most valuable company in the United States. Its stock price fell 3 percent on Friday, dropping its market value to about 3.4 trillion dollars. Alphabet, the parent company of Google, is now worth about 3.44 trillion dollars. This decline marks Nvidia’s seventh straight day of losses. The sell-off follows the recent resignation of Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang. The broader tech market also struggled, as the Nasdaq Composite dropped 5.3 percent. The S&P 500 fell 3.7 percent, entering what analysts call correction territory.

President Donald Trump announced plans to penalize U.S. tech companies that build AI data centers in other countries. He stated that he wants to prevent these companies from moving overseas. The president suggested that China would otherwise take control of the technology. Trump made this announcement after returning from a trilateral summit in China with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping. The president did not provide details on how the government would enforce these penalties. Some members of the president's own team said they were hearing about this potential policy for the first time.

In climate news, negotiations at the COP31 UN summit in Turkey remain in a deadlock. Countries are struggling to agree on a new global climate deal. A group of nations led by France and Panama is pushing for a commitment to reduce the world's demand for fossil fuels. Saudi Arabia and other fossil fuel producers have opposed these mentions in the draft agreement. Meanwhile, the Africa Group is demanding more funding for climate adaptation. The current draft acknowledges that the goal of keeping global temperature rise below 1.5 degrees Celsius has been missed. A final agreement is expected to be published on Saturday.

A transcription company called Tigerfish has secured its data after a security lapse exposed private information online. The San Francisco-based company processes audio and video for police, prosecutors, and tech firms. A security researcher named Anurag Sen found the data on an Amazon-hosted cloud server. He reported that the files were accessible to anyone on the internet without a password. The exposed data included police interviews and body-cam footage. Tigerfish president Adam Goldberg said the company has now blocked all public access to the server. He added that the company is reviewing its storage security.

Turning to the conflict in Ukraine, a U.S. official says Russia is showing openness to NATO-like security guarantees for Ukraine. This would be part of a potential peace deal if current front lines are frozen. U.S. special envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff have been meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Berlin. President Trump also participated in these discussions following his trip to China. The proposal would offer security commitments similar to NATO’s Article 5 without formal membership. Russia has demanded to keep the territories it has already captured. The U.S. official says Washington aims to keep Ukraine sovereign and secure.

Next, the European Union and the United Kingdom have struck a landmark deal to strengthen their ties after Brexit.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham met with European Union officials in Brussels on Friday. They discussed rebuilding economic and political ties between the UK and the European Union. This summit happened ten years after the UK voted to leave the bloc. The UK officially exited the European Union in twenty twenty. Prime Minister Burnham stated that leaving the bloc has not worked for the country. He wants to secure deals to ease the movement of goods and people. The two sides discussed ways to potentially get back together. The Prime Minister has returned to the UK with a potential new deal.

China’s budget reached a surplus in October because of a tax enforcement campaign. Government revenue exceeded spending by two hundred sixty-five point seven billion yuan. That equals about thirty-nine point eight billion dollars. This was the first surplus for China in one year. The government collected more than two hundred ninety-six billion yuan in individual income tax. This is an increase of nearly ninety percent from one year ago. Beijing is now monitoring offshore trusts set up by citizens to improve tax compliance. Tax payments on offshore trust income rose after a late October deadline. The government also increased spending on national infrastructure projects.

Hackers breached a US Department of Agriculture system used to pay farmers. The incident happened earlier this week, according to a report by NBC News. The breach affected a database that handles loans, insurance, and assistance payments. The department notified employees about the security incident on Thursday. Officials said no personal information or data was lost in the breach. The department's cybersecurity team detected the incident and reset passwords for all databases. This caused outages for financial tools used by farmers. Agriculture Undersecretary Richard Fordyce confirmed the cyberthreat on Friday. Most systems were expected to be restored by the end of the day.

The FBI is investigating a suspected breach of a nationwide criminal justice database. CNN reported the breach on November twentieth, citing two people familiar with the investigation. The database is used by local, state, and federal agencies to share information. It contains records on warrants, criminal histories, and background checks. This is the second intrusion involving an FBI system in recent months. A group called ShinyHunters accessed an FBI jobs website in September. That breach compromised data on current and former FBI employees. The agency has not responded to requests for comment.

A UK tribunal ruled that the government cannot keep an Apple encryption order secret. The Home Office had argued that confirming the order would hurt national security. The Investigatory Powers Tribunal rejected that claim on Thursday. The order is a technical capability notice under the Investigatory Powers Act of twenty sixteen. It can require companies to change their services so authorities can access data. The judges noted that government sources had already confirmed the order to the press. The ruling does not make the content of the order public. A full hearing is expected in the first half of twenty twenty-seven.

Scientists believe they have discovered where the brain plans out speech. Dr. Eddie Chang of the University of California, San Francisco, led the study. Researchers monitored twenty-eight patients during epilepsy surgery to track brain activity. They focused on an area called Wernicke’s area, located above the left ear. Textbooks previously said this area was only for understanding sounds. The study found that this area also plans words before a person speaks. It sends signals to the vocal tract a split second before speaking. This finding could help experts understand speech difficulties in children. It may also improve devices used by people with paralysis.

Before we go, here is your thought for the day.

You carry biological memories from ancestors you never met. Biology once suggested that only your own life experiences shaped your traits. New findings show that intense life events can leave chemical marks on your DNA. These molecular tags act like switches for your genes. When an ancestor survives a famine or great fear, they pass down a biological instruction manual. This prepares your body to react to similar dangers before you are born. You arrive in the world with instincts fine-tuned by the hardships of your ancestors. You are a living archive of your family history. If your biology remembers the past, how might your own experiences change the future?

Thanks for listening to the Sift Daily Briefing.

audioBriefIndepth.script:
Welcome to your Sift In-Depth Briefing. This is your full analysis of the day’s most important developments.

Why are lawmakers worried about where our most advanced computer chips are going? The United States is concerned that powerful artificial intelligence chips are reaching countries that might share them with China.

These chips are the engines that power modern artificial intelligence. They process massive amounts of information at lightning speed. Because they are so valuable, the United States has strict rules about who can buy them. The goal is to keep this technology out of the hands of rivals.

Recently, the government discovered a loophole. Companies were using data centers in places like Thailand and Indonesia to access American computing power from afar. This allowed them to bypass existing rules. Now, the government says customers in those countries must get a special permit to buy these chips.

This move follows a tense investigation into a company based in Singapore. Officials believe it may have helped move restricted Nvidia chips into China. While the government tries to tighten these rules, some lawmakers say it is not enough. They want even tougher oversight on how these chips travel across the globe.

This is happening now because the government is under pressure to prove it can control its own technology. With a new Congress taking power in January, leaders are promising to investigate how many chips have already reached Chinese firms.

For you, this means the global market for high-tech parts is becoming more complicated. You might see companies struggle to keep up with changing rules. Keep an eye on whether these new permits actually stop the chips from reaching China, or if companies find new ways around them.

The struggle to control technology is also shaking up the stock market. Why did shares of the chipmaker Nvidia suddenly lose so much value? Investors are worried that the massive spending on artificial intelligence might not pay off as quickly as they hoped.

Nvidia is a company that makes the specialized chips needed to build artificial intelligence. For a long time, its stock price climbed higher and higher. It became one of the most valuable companies in the world. Investors believed that AI would change everything, so they poured money into the business.

But recently, the mood on Wall Street changed. People started asking if companies were spending too much money too fast. They also grew nervous after the company’s co-founder and leader, Jensen Huang, resigned. Without his familiar leadership, investors began to wonder what the future of the company would look like.

The situation turned into news when Nvidia’s stock price dropped sharply for several days in a row. This decline was so deep that Nvidia lost its spot as the third-most valuable company in the United States. It fell behind Alphabet, which owns Google.

This drop triggered a wider panic across the stock market. Because Nvidia is so important to the tech industry, its fall dragged down other companies too. Major stock indexes like the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq fell significantly. This left many investors feeling worried that the excitement around AI might be a financial bubble.

This is happening now because the market is shifting its focus. Instead of just wanting growth at any cost, investors are now demanding to see real profits. They are looking at the huge amounts of money spent on data centers and wondering when that money will come back.

For you, this means your retirement account or other investments might see some bumps in the road. When tech stocks drop this much, it often affects the whole economy. Watch to see if companies can prove they are making money from their AI tools, or if the market continues to slide.

The pressure on these companies is growing even more as the government changes the rules for where they can build. Why is the president threatening to tax companies that build their computer centers in other countries? He wants to force tech giants to bring those projects back to the United States.

Data centers are the giant warehouses that house the powerful computers needed for AI. These buildings need a lot of land and a huge amount of electricity. Because they can be noisy and use so much power, many people who live near them do not want them in their neighborhoods.

To avoid these local fights, many tech companies have built their data centers in other countries. It is often cheaper and easier to find space abroad. Companies also want to be closer to the people using their services in those regions.

The situation changed when the president announced a new plan. He said he would ban companies from building these centers abroad. If they do it anyway, he threatened to hit them with a "tremendous tax." He believes these centers are valuable assets that should stay on American soil.

This news came as a surprise to many, including some of his own staff. The president said he wants these projects to go to places in the United States that need the work, like Texas or West Virginia. He encouraged local leaders to find ways to make these companies pay for the right to build in their towns.

This is happening now because the president is trying to balance national pride with the reality of building new technology. He wants to ensure the United States remains the leader in AI. He also met recently with leaders in China, which has kept the focus on how countries compete for digital power.

For you, this means you might see more of these giant buildings popping up near your own community. You could also see higher costs for tech services if companies are forced to build in more expensive locations. Watch to see if companies change their plans, or if they decide to pay the tax to keep building where they want.

The fight over fossil fuels leaves COP31 climate talks in deadlock.

Why are climate change talks in Turkey stuck in a deadlock? Countries are fighting over whether to include a promise to move away from fossil fuels in their final agreement.

For years, nations have met at these summits to address global warming. They want to keep the Earth’s temperature from rising more than one and a half degrees Celsius. This goal is vital because crossing it means more extreme heat and rising seas for everyone. Recently, the world officially entered a period called "overshoot," where we have already missed that temperature target.

Negotiators were working on a document called the Antalya Accords. An earlier version included plans to move away from oil, gas, and coal. But a new draft removed those direct mentions of fossil fuels. This change happened after countries that produce these fuels, led by Saudi Arabia, pushed for their removal.

Now, a group of countries led by France and Panama is refusing to accept the new draft. They say it is unacceptable to ignore the main cause of climate change. Meanwhile, the Africa Group is also unhappy. They are calling for more money to help their people adapt to the changing climate, saying they did not come to the summit to beg. COP31 President Chris Bowen is defending the draft. He argues the summit should focus on moving toward clean energy sources instead.

This is happening now because the summit is reaching its final hours. Negotiators must decide whether to put fossil fuel language back into the text before the meeting ends.

For the world, this means the outcome could determine how seriously countries take cutting emissions. If the final deal omits fossil fuels, some experts fear it will be a step backward for climate action. You should watch to see if diplomats can find a compromise that satisfies both the countries wanting stronger climate rules and those focused on energy production.

Next, let us look at a security mistake that left private information wide open.

Why did a company that works with police and tech giants accidentally share its customers' private files with the entire internet? The company left a digital storage folder unlocked, meaning no password was needed to see the data inside.

This company, called Tigerfish, turns audio and video into written text. Their customers include government offices, police departments, and large tech companies. To store all these files, they use cloud servers, which are essentially giant digital filing cabinets hosted by companies like Amazon.

In October, a security researcher named Anurag Sen found that one of these digital cabinets was not locked. He discovered that anyone with the right web address could look at sensitive files. These files included police interviews, body-cam footage, and private invoices. Sen has spent years looking for these kinds of mistakes to help companies fix them before bad actors find them.

The company secured the folder soon after being contacted. Tigerfish president Adam Goldberg said the company's email about the leak was caught in a spam filter. He added that they are now reviewing their security to make sure no other folders are left open.

This happened because of what experts call basic human error. It is common for engineers to turn off security settings while testing a new system and then forget to turn them back on.

For the listener, this shows how fragile our digital world can be. Even big companies that handle sensitive government data can make simple mistakes that put privacy at risk. You might watch for whether companies start using better automated tools to prevent these human errors before they happen.

Finally, we turn to the war in Ukraine and the difficult search for a peace deal.

Is Russia willing to accept security guarantees for Ukraine if the fighting stops? A U.S. official says Russia is showing more openness to the idea, but only if current battle lines are frozen in place.

For nearly five years, Russia and Ukraine have been locked in a major conflict. Ukraine wants to join NATO, the military alliance where an attack on one member is an attack on all. Russia has strongly opposed this, fearing NATO's influence near its borders. U.S. negotiators Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff have been meeting with leaders to find a way to end the fighting.

The proposal they are discussing would give Ukraine "NATO-like" security. This would mean other countries promise to defend Ukraine if it is attacked, but without Ukraine officially joining the NATO alliance. The U.S. official says the goal is to keep Ukraine secure without using the NATO brand. Russia, however, wants to keep the territories it has already captured.

A Russian official, Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov, pushed back on this idea. He called any form of NATO-style guarantee for Ukraine totally unacceptable. He said Russia’s main demand remains that Ukraine must never join the alliance. Still, reports suggest that European leaders are planning a visit to Russia to clarify these positions.

This is happening now because the Trump administration is working hard to broker an end to the war. Both sides remain far apart on issues of land and long-term security.

For the world, this means a peace deal remains very difficult to reach. President Trump has noted that there is deep hatred between the two leaders, which makes talking even harder. You should watch to see if these diplomatic visits to Moscow lead to any change in Russia's position on security guarantees.

Negotiators from the European Union and the United Kingdom are now working to finalize a landmark deal to strengthen their ties following Brexit.

Can Britain and the European Union find a way to work together again after years of being apart? The United Kingdom and the European Union have held a rare meeting to sign new agreements that bring the two sides closer together.

A decade ago, the people of Britain voted to leave the European Union. This group of twenty-seven countries works together on laws, trade, and travel. Britain had been a member for a long time, but the country decided to exit, a process known as Brexit. This caused a lot of trouble for trade and travel between Britain and its neighbors. Since then, the two sides have struggled to agree on how to handle their relationship.

Now, Prime Minister Andy Burnham is working to fix some of those problems. He believes the original Brexit plan did not work well for Britain. He wants to make things easier for people and businesses.

The two sides met in Brussels to sign a set of new deals. One deal allows up to one hundred thousand young adults from Britain to live and work in Europe for three years. The same number of Europeans can move to Britain. They also agreed to make it easier to trade food and farm products. This should help keep prices down at the grocery store.

This is happening now because both sides feel they need each other more than before. The war in Ukraine has made security a big priority for everyone in Europe. Britain has a strong military, and the European Union wants to work with them to stay safe.

Some people in Britain worry that these deals mean the country is giving up its independence. They fear Britain might eventually try to rejoin the European Union entirely. For now, the agreements aim to make daily life a little easier, but we will have to watch to see if this leads to a deeper, more permanent connection.

Trade and politics are not the only things governments are watching closely, as tax collectors in China have found a new way to fill the country's bank accounts.

Has China’s government found a new way to collect more money from its citizens? Yes, the government launched a strict campaign to tax offshore wealth, which gave the country a rare budget surplus last month.

For a long time, many wealthy people in China moved their money into offshore trusts. These are legal arrangements kept in other countries to manage money and avoid certain taxes. The Chinese government has been looking for ways to make more money because they are not selling as much land as they used to. Selling land had been a big way for the government to earn cash.

The government started a very strict tax enforcement campaign. They used better technology to find money that was hidden in these offshore trusts. They told people they had until late October to pay what they owed or face extra charges. Because of this, many people rushed to pay their taxes.

This caused a huge amount of money to flow into the government's pockets. In just one month, the government collected over two hundred ninety-six billion yuan in individual income tax. That is nearly ninety percent more than they collected at this time last year. This helped the government have more money than it spent, creating a surplus for the first time in a year.

This is happening now because the government needs to pay for new national projects, like building better roads and power grids. They are also trying to fix the economy after a slowdown in the housing market.

While the government has more money now, the rest of the economy is still struggling. Investment in businesses and property is down quite a bit. Experts suggest the government might save some of this extra money to help the economy grow in the coming years.

Government money is also at the center of a new security problem in the United States.

How did hackers get into a system used to send money to American farmers? Hackers broke into a database at the United States Department of Agriculture that handles loans and insurance payments.

The Department of Agriculture, or USDA, helps farmers across the country. They provide loans to help them buy land or equipment. They also help with insurance if crops fail. To do this, the department uses large computer systems to track payments and keep records.

Earlier this week, employees noticed that these systems were not working properly. The department’s computer team saw a security incident and had to reset passwords to stop the hackers. This caused the computer systems to shut down, which meant farmers could not check their loan status or get their payments.

Officials at the department confirmed that hackers did break into the payment system. While this was a serious problem, they said that no private information about farmers was stolen. They believe the systems designed to protect data worked as they should.

This is happening now because the department has been struggling to keep its computer systems safe. A government report released this week found that the USDA and other agencies have not met all the rules for good cybersecurity. They often do not have enough staff or money to keep up with the latest threats.

Most of the systems are expected to be fixed soon, but the department has more work to do to keep hackers out in the future. We will have to wait to see if the department can better protect its information, including sensitive research on animal diseases.
